title.en: Who is Natalie Harp, Trump's right-hand woman?
title.zh: 谁是特朗普的得力助手娜塔莉·哈普？

summary.en: Natalie Harp, a long-serving and loyal aide to former President Trump, gained renewed public attention after a Democrat senator highlighted her close relationship with the president.
summary.zh: 娜塔莉·哈普是前总统特朗普任职时间最长、最忠诚的助手之一，在一位民主党参议员指出她与总统的亲密关系后，她再次受到公众关注。

body.en:
Few people in US President Donald Trump's orbit have appeared as frequently by his side as Natalie Harp in recent years.

One of Trump's longest-serving and most loyal aides, 35-year-old Harp is trusted with typing out his Truth Social posts, among other top responsibilities.

She was thrust again into the spotlight this week by Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff - a Democrat and frequent Trump foil - when he name-checked her during a speech that has since gone viral.

Ossoff attacked Trump's "travel with Natalie on their apparently defenceless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar", referring to the new Air Force One plane as well as to reports that Harp joined Trump - and a small group of people - when he secretly swapped planes leaving Turkey last month.

Here is what you need to know about the Trump assistant who has been called both a "gatekeeper" and a "comfort blanket".

A California native and member of a conservative Christian family, Harp followed an unorthodox path into an already unconventional White House.

In his first term, Trump got the Right to Try Act passed to give some patients greater access to experimental treatments, which Harp used for her bone cancer.

She quickly gained prominence and popularity in Trump's Maga (Make America Great Again) wing of the Republican party by talking about the experience, and soon after joined an advisory board for Trump's 2020 re-election campaign.

"When I failed the chemotherapies that were on the market, no-one wanted me in their clinical trials," she said at the 2020 Republican National Convention.

"They didn't give me the right to try experimental treatments, Mr President. You did, and without you, I'd have died waiting for them to be approved."

After the event, Trump said: "She lit up the television screen like very few people I have ever seen do it."

Following Trump's loss in that election, Harp found work hosting a show at the conservative One America News Network, or OAN.

There, she became known as a ferocious Trump defender and promoter of false claims that he won the 2020 election. She left the network in 2022 to join Trump's next presidential campaign.

Most accounts of Trump's views of Harp come via anonymous second-hand sources in books by reporters such as Maggie Haberman, Jonathan Swan or Michael Wolff, and very little is publicly known about her private life.

"Trump is like everything that my mom taught us to respect," her brother Preston Harp said during a CNN , external interview on Tuesday. "So I think that's where her infatuation for Trump comes from honestly."

Noting an emphasis on American exceptionalism in their upbringing, he added that Harp was fixated on the White House from a young age and wrote letters to previous presidents, including George W Bush during the Iraq...
body.zh: 近年来，在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的圈子里，很少有人能像娜塔莉·哈普那样频繁地出现在他身边。 35 岁的哈普是特朗普任职时间最长、最忠诚的助手之一，他被信任负责撰写他的《真相社会》帖子以及其他重要职责。 本周，佐治亚州参议员乔恩·奥索夫（Jon Ossoff）再次将她推到了聚光灯下。乔恩·奥索夫是民主党人，也是特朗普的常客。他最近在一场演讲中点名了她，这场演讲后来迅速走红。 奥索夫攻击特朗普“与娜塔莉一起乘坐卡塔尔埃米尔赠送的显然毫无防备的飞行宫殿”，他指的是新的空军一号飞机，以及有关哈普上个月秘密换乘飞机离开土耳其时与特朗普和一小群人一起的报道。 关于这位被称为“看门人”和“安慰毯”的特朗普助手，你需要了解以下信息。 哈普是加州人，出身于一个保守的基督教家庭，他沿着一条非正统的道路进入了已经非常规的白宫。 在特朗普的第一个任期内，特朗普通过了《尝试权法案》，让一些患者有更多机会获得实验性治疗，哈普曾用这种方法治疗她的骨癌。谈论这段经历后，她很快在共和党特朗普的 Maga（让美国再次伟大）派系中获得了知名度和声望，并很快加入了特朗普 2020 年连任竞选的顾问委员会。 她在 2020 年共和党全国代表大会上表示：“当市场上的化疗失败时，没有人希望我参加他们的临床试验。” “总统先生，他们没有给我尝试实验性治疗的权利。你做到了，如果没有你，我就会在等待他们获得批准的过程中死去。” 活动结束后，特朗普表示：“她点亮了电视屏幕，我见过很少有人能做到这一点。” 特朗普在那次选举中失利后，哈普找到了在保守派的一个美国人新闻网 (OAN) 主持节目的工作。 在那里，她被称为凶猛的特朗普捍卫者和著名的选举否认者。她于 2022 年离开该网络，参加特朗普的下一届总统竞选活动。 大多数关于特朗普对哈普的看法的描述都来自玛吉·哈伯曼、乔纳森·斯旺或迈克尔·沃尔夫等记者所著书籍中的匿名二手资料，而公众对她的私生活知之甚少。 现在，哈普在白宫的正式头衔是总统行政助理，这通常表示较低级别的职位，需要管理后勤、日程安排、通讯流程和平凡但至关重要的秘书工作。 不过，从各方面来看，哈普赋予了这一角色新的含义，她的知名度明显高于她的前任，例如特朗普第一届政府中的玛德琳·韦斯特豪特。 记者在...

reflection.en: The story of Natalie Harp highlights the significant role of trusted advisors and loyal aides in leadership. While the nature of counsel can vary, the biblical principle reminds us that leaders benefit from a multitude of perspectives. In any sphere of influence, wise guidance is crucial for stability and success.
reflection.zh: 娜塔莉·哈普的故事突显了值得信赖的顾问和忠诚助手在领导层中的重要作用。虽然建议的性质可能各不相同，但圣经原则提醒我们，领导者从众多的视角中受益。在任何影响领域，明智的指导对于稳定和成功都至关重要。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Australia 'outraged' after Israeli decision not to prosecute over killing of aid worker in Gaza
title.zh: 澳大利亚对以色列决定不起诉加沙援助人员遇害案表示“愤怒”

summary.en: Australia's foreign minister expressed outrage and plans to summon the Israeli ambassador following Israel's decision not to prosecute those responsible for the killing of aid worker Zomi Frankcom in Gaza. The minister described the decision as "insulting."
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长表示，以色列决定不起诉在加沙杀害援助人员佐米·弗兰克科姆的责任人，澳方对此感到“愤怒”，并将召见以色列大使。部长称这项决定是“侮辱性的”。

body.en:
Australia's foreign minister has said she is "outraged" over an Israeli government decision not to prosecute those responsible for the death of aid worker Zomi Frankcom, who was killed in an IDF strike.

Frankcom was an Australian aid worker with World Central Kitchen (WCK) who was killed in Gaza with six other colleagues by an Israeli airstrike in April 2024.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the decision "falls far short of the accountability we expect" and that she would call in the Israeli ambassador.

Australia would continue pressing Israel "for justice for Zomi and her colleagues", she said in a statement on Thursday.

Wong said the Australian government had learned of Israel's decision late on Wednesday night, adding that the outcome was "especially insulting" as it occurred on World Humanitarian Day.

"This is despite Israel Defense Forces admissions that the IDF strikes on Zomi and her colleagues' vehicles were the result of serious failures to follow IDF procedures, mistaken identification and errors in decision-making," she said.

Wong said the government would continue pressing Israel "for justice for Zomi and her colleagues".

"I will call in Israel's Ambassador to Australia Hillel Newman and have directed Australia's Ambassador to Israel to convey our views directly to Israel as the Australian Government considers next steps."

Wong's comments mark one of the strongest censures of the Israeli military by Australia since the war in Gaza began, reflecting broader international condemnation of the WCK attack .

Australian former defence force chief Mark Binskin handed down a report in August 2024 that found "serious failures" in the IDF's procedures led to the killing of Frankcom. Three British nationals, a Palestinian, a Pole and a dual US-Canadian citizen were also killed in the attack.

The IDF's Frankcom decision contrasts with its separate announcement that it would carry out a criminal investigation into the killing of five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab in Gaza in 2024.

Israel's military said that its soldiers opened fire at the ambulance in which she was being transported after suffering injuries in an earlier attack.
body.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长表示，她对以色列政府决定不起诉那些在以色列国防军袭击中丧生的援助人员佐米·弗兰克科姆之死的责任人感到“愤怒”。 Frankcom 是世界中央厨房 (WCK) 的一名澳大利亚援助人员，2024 年 4 月，他与其他六名同事在加沙遭到以色列空袭身亡。 外交部长黄英贤表示，这一决定“远远低于我们期望的问责制”，她将传唤以色列大使。 她在周四的一份声明中表示，澳大利亚将继续向以色列施压，“为佐米及其同事伸张正义”。 黄说，澳大利亚政府在周三深夜获悉以色列的决定，并补充说，这一结果“尤其具有侮辱性”，因为它发生在世界人道主义日。 她说：“尽管以色列国防军承认，以色列国防军对佐米及其同事车辆的袭击是由于严重不遵守以色列国防军程序、错误识别和决策失误造成的。” 黄表示，政府将继续向以色列施压，“为佐米和她的同事伸张正义”。 “我将召见以色列驻澳大利亚大使希勒尔·纽曼，并指示澳大利亚驻以色列大使在澳大利亚政府考虑下一步行动时直接向以色列转达我们的观点。” 黄的言论是自加沙战争爆发以来澳大利亚对以色列军方最强烈的谴责之一，反映出国际社会对 WCK 袭击事件的更广泛谴责。 澳大利亚前国防军参谋长马克·宾斯金 (Mark Binskin) 于 2024 年 8 月提交了一份报告，发现以色列国防军的程序存在“严重失误”，导致 Frankcom 被杀。三名英国国民、一名巴勒斯坦人、一名波兰人和一名美国加拿大双重公民也在袭击中丧生。 以色列国防军 Frankcom 的决定与以色列国防军单独宣布将对 2024 年在加沙杀害 5 岁巴勒斯坦女孩 Hind Rajab 进行刑事调查形成鲜明对比。 以色列军方表示，在早些时候的袭击中受伤后，以色列士兵向运送她的救护车开枪。

reflection.en: The news of an aid worker's death and the subsequent decision not to prosecute evokes a deep sense of injustice, echoing the prophet Habakkuk's lament. When accountability seems to falter, it can feel as though justice is paralyzed, leading to profound outrage and diplomatic protest. In such moments, we are reminded of the human longing for righteousness...
reflection.zh: 援助人员遇害后，不起诉相关责任人的决定引发了强烈的不公感，这与先知哈巴谷的哀叹不谋而合。当问责似乎失效时，人们会感到公义被阻碍，从而引发极大的愤怒和外交抗议。在这样的时刻，我们被提醒人类对公义的渴望，以及所有国家维护公义的呼召。

verse.textEn: The law is paralyzed, and justice never prevails. The wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.
verse.textZh: 因此律法放松，公理也不显明；恶人围困义人，所以公理显然颠倒。

title.en: Ecuador intelligence chief and five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash
title.zh: 厄瓜多尔情报局长和五名美国人在肯尼亚直升机失事中丧生

summary.en: Michele Sensi-Contugi, and his wife Stephany Hollihan among the seven people killed in the crash.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Ecuador's intelligence chief and his wife have been killed in a helicopter crash in Kenya.

Michele Sensi-Contugi and his wife Stephany Hollihan were among the seven people killed when the accident happened in Samburu county at approximately 09:13 (06:13 GMT) on Wednesday.

The Kenya Civil Aviation Authority (KCAA) said the helicopter was on a scenic flight from a wildlife conservancy in Loisaba to Ewaso Nyiro, a river that flows along several national reserves.

Samburu county is a popular tourist destination with many private wildlife conservancies and is renowned for its stunning landscape.

Images from the scene show smoke at the wooded crash site on Mount Ololokwe, as members of the Kenya Red Cross approach the still-burning wreckage.

Ecuador has not given details about the death of Sensi-Contugi, 44, who was named director general of the Strategic Intelligence Center in 2024.

The president's office led tributes on behalf of the government to express sadness over the death of the intelligence chief.

Former President of Ecuador Guillermo Lasso mentioned he had died in the helicopter crash.

Lady Lori Helicopters, which operated the the Eurocopter EC130 B4 aircraft, said it was "deeply saddened" by the accident.

"Our deepest sympathies are with the guests, crew, their families and loved ones, and all those affected by this tragic accident," a statement read.

According to a memo seen by the BBC's US partner CBS News , external one of the Americans killed in the crash was NBCUniversal journalist José Alberto Suárez.

In the memo, NBCUniversal called Suárez "a deeply respected leader and beloved friend and colleague.

Miami restaurateur Roger Duarte was among the Americans killed in the crash, according to local and US media.

Commenting on his death on X, US Rep Carlos Antonio Gimenez wrote: "Our prayers are with their loved ones during this incredibly difficult time. May their memories be a blessing."

Earlier reports had suggested seven people, six tourists and a pilot, were killed in the crash.

In February, a helicopter crash in the Rift Valley county of Nandi killed six people, including a member of parliament.

In 2024, the military chief, Gen Francis Omondi Ogolla, died after an army helicopter that was carrying 11 people crashed in the west of the country, with only two survivors.

In June 2021 at least 10 soldiers were killed when their helicopter crashed while landing near the capital, Nairobi.
body.zh: 厄瓜多尔情报局长和他的妻子在肯尼亚的一次直升机失事中丧生。 星期三上午 9 点 13 分（格林威治标准时间 06 点 13 分）左右，桑布鲁县发生了这起事故，其中 Michele Sensi-Contugi 和他的妻子 Stephany Hollihan 是遇难者之一。 肯尼亚民航局（KCAA）表示，这架直升机正在从洛伊萨巴野生动物保护区飞往埃瓦索尼罗河（Ewaso Nyiro）的观光飞行中，埃瓦索尼罗河是一条流经多个国家保护区的河流。 桑布鲁县是一个受欢迎的旅游目的地，拥有许多私人野生动物保护区，并以其令人惊叹的景观而闻名。 现场图像显示，当肯尼亚红十字会成员接近仍在燃烧的残骸时，奥洛洛奎山树木繁茂的坠机现场冒出浓烟。 厄瓜多尔尚未提供 44 岁的森西-孔图吉 (Sensi-Contugi) 去世的详细信息，他于 2024 年被任命为战略情报中心主任。 总统办公室代表政府举行悼念活动，对情报局长的去世表示哀悼。 厄瓜多尔前总统吉列尔莫·拉索表示，他在直升机失事中丧生。 运营欧洲直升机公司 EC130 B4 飞机的 Lady Lori Helicopters 表示，对这起事故“深感悲痛”。 一份声明中写道：“我们向客人、船员、他们的家人和亲人以及所有受到这场悲惨事故影响的人表示最深切的同情。” 根据BBC美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司新闻网看到的一份备忘录，在此次事故中丧生的美国人之一是NBC环球记者何塞·阿尔贝托·苏亚雷斯。 在备忘录中，NBCUniversal 称苏亚雷斯是“一位深受尊敬的领导人、挚爱的朋友和同事。 据当地和美国媒体报道，迈阿密餐馆老板罗杰·杜阿尔特是在此次事故中丧生的美国人之一。 美国众议员卡洛斯·安东尼奥·吉梅内斯 (Carlos Antonio Gimenez) 在 X 上评论他的去世时写道：“在这个极其困难的时刻，我们为他们的亲人祈祷。愿他们的回忆成为祝福。” 早些时候的报道称，事故中有七人死亡，其中包括六名游客和一名飞行员。 2月，南迪裂谷县发生的一次直升机坠毁事件造成六人死亡，其中包括一名议员。 2024 年，一架载有 11 人的军用直升机在该国西部坠毁，军事首长弗朗西斯·奥蒙迪·奥古拉 (Francis Omondi Ogolla) 将军身亡，只有两名幸存者。 2021 年 6 月，至少 10 名士兵乘坐的直升机在首都内罗毕附近降落时坠毁。

title.en: 'I get along with him': Trump says he'll meet with North Korea's Kim Jong Un
title.zh: “我和他相处融洽”：特朗普表示他将与朝鲜金正恩会面

summary.en: In an unusual move, Trump also cited a specific number of warheads that he said North Korea holds.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump says he ‌plans to meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, saying that the Asian ‌nation holds 57 "very powerful" nuclear weapons.

The remarks come as Trump ordered Pentagon officials to ‌cut short joint exercises with the South Korean military.

He wrote in a Sunday social media post that they sent a message to North Korea that was "totally inappropriate and hostile, to a Country that, as long as Donald J. Trump has been President, ‌has been unthreatening and ‌respectful".

During Trump's ⁠first term, Kim called Trump a "mentally deranged US dotard" and threatened that he had use of a "nuclear button" on his desk.

But the two leaders turned that tension into face-to-face meetings, including a brief exchange at the demilitarised zone between the Koreas in which Trump became the first sitting US president to step into North Korean territory.

The leaders' relationship cooled after the face-to-face meetings in 2018 and 2019 .

"I ‌know Kim Jong Un very well, and he's going to be fine as long as we have ‌a smart president," Trump told reporters during a tour of the helipad he is constructing on the White House's historic south lawn.

"I get along with him well," Trump said. "And you know what? The fact that I get along with him, that’s a very good thing, not a bad thing."

"He has 57 very powerful nuclear weapons They should have ‌never allowed it. If I were president, I wouldn't have allowed it. But he's got them," Trump said.

Trump's citing of a specific number of nuclear weapons held by North Korea was highly unusual.

There have been varying estimates by experts over the years on how many nuclear weapons North Korea has.

The US government does not publicly publish an official estimate of North Korea's nuclear arsenal, although a 2025 report by the Congressional Research Service cited non-governmental experts as estimating that North Korea has produced enough fissile material for up to 90 warheads but may have assembled approximately 50.

In June, the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute estimated that North Korea has "possibly assembled around 60 warheads, possesses enough fissile material to produce at ⁠least 30 more".

title.en: Sacked Ukrainian defence minister calls for presidential election
title.zh: 被解雇的乌克兰国防部长呼吁举行总统选举

summary.en: Martial law has been in place in Ukraine since February 2022, under which elections are suspended.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Ukraine's popular ex-defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov has called for wartime elections, in what is widely seen as the biggest challenge to Volodymyr Zelensky's presidency since Russia's full-scale invasion four and a half years ago.

"Democracy cannot be held hostage by Russia," said Fedorov, 35, in a video posted to YouTube on Tuesday, adding that Ukraine is fighting "precisely because we want to remain a free European state".

Since the war broke out in 2022 Ukraine has been under martial law, meaning elections are suspended.

Fedorov, who did not mention Zelensky by name in the video, was unexpectedly fired from his role as defence minister last month, just six months after his appointment.

Zelensky has not directly responded to the video from Fedorov, whose dismissal sparked protests across the country .

But in his own video message late on Wednesday, the Ukrainian president mentioned the tasks the newly-confirmed Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara faced, including defending against deadly Russian aerial attacks and expanding Ukraine's "deep-strike capabilities" inside Russia.

Meanwhile, a source in the presidential office told the BBC it was "highly bizarre to plan elections amidst missiles and drones. This demonstrates a complete lack of realism".

A number of Ukrainian analysts have also questioned whether it would be possible to properly organise the voting for millions of Ukrainians who have fled the country and also hundreds of thousands of soldiers on the front line.

Zelensky - whose five-year presidential term ended in May 2024 - has been under pressure from both Washington and Moscow to hold new elections.

When US President Donald Trump suggested last year that Kyiv was "using war" to avoid a vote, Zelensky said Ukraine was "ready for elections" within 60-90 days if its allies helped guarantee security for them.

Holding a fair and safe vote would present considerable challenges for a country under repeated Russian bombardment and many Ukrainians saw Trump's remarks as reflecting Vladimir Putin's narrative that Zelensky is not a legitimate leader.

In the latest Russian attacks on Wednesday, four people were killed when a drone hit a minibus in the southern city of Kherson. Buses and minibuses in Kherson have been repeatedly targeted in recent months, killing drivers and passengers alike.

In the central city of Zhytomyr, two police officers were killed and another 20 people injured in a Russian drone strike on the regional police headquarters, a local official said.

In a separate development , Ukraine's two anti-corruption agencies said they were conducting a special operation targeting current and former MPs as well as an unnamed official in the presidential office.

title.en: Canada and US say they are finalising a trade deal, but details remain murky
title.zh: 加拿大和美国称正在敲定贸易协议，但细节仍不明朗

summary.en: Prime Minister Carney announced significant progress in trade talks between Canada and the US, as both nations work to finalize details before a looming tariff deadline this weekend.
summary.zh: 加拿大总理卡尼宣布，两国贸易谈判取得“重大进展”，双方正努力在新的周末关税截止日期前敲定最终细节。

body.en:
Canada and the US are finalising a highly anticipated trade deal, with President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Mark Carney touting it as a success.

Trump said the proposed deal will be welcome by US farmers and manufacturers, while Carney said it will secure "the best terms" for Canada's strategic sectors and provide certainty on the future of US-Canada trade.

Trade negotiators met on Wednesday for the third time in as many days on Wednesday and after Trump paused a new wave of tariffs he had threatened to impose overnight on a range of Canadian goods.

But details on what the agreement covers, what concessions both sides have made, and what still needs to be ironed out, remain unclear.

Speaking to reporters briefly on Wednesday after a 45-minute meeting with his Canadian counterpart, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the Americans are "very happy" with the latest discussions.

"We feel confident that we've reached an agreement that will not only continue to protect American workers, American jobs, American supply chains, but really strengthen the North American economy," Greer said.

The deal eliminates "some of the irritants" that the US has had with Canada, he added.

Trump said Canada has agreed to eliminate tariffs on US farmers, though he did not specify which specific agricultural sectors would benefit.

Asked whether the US will also be reducing some tariffs it has placed on Canada, Trump said by "a little bit".

In a post on X, Carney congratulated Greer and Canada-US Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc "for the significant progress" made in negotiations.

"We are now moving towards an agreement that reinforces that Canadian advantage, including by securing the best terms in each of Canada's most important strategic sectors and providing greater certainty about our future trading relationship," Carney wrote on Wednesday.

The prime minister is meeting with his cabinet and leaders of Canadian provinces on Wednesday afternoon to brief them on the deal.

LeBlanc and his team have been camped out in Washington for more than a week to hammer out a deal ahead of a wave of new 50% tariffs the Trump administration planned to implement on Wednesday. Those have now been paused until the weekend.

Canada has been in pursuit of a deal that would have the US drop or reduce tariffs on its steel, aluminium, automobiles and lumber.

The US, meanwhile, has been asking for a number of concessions from Canada, including removing its remaining retaliatory tariffs on American autos and adjusting its dairy quotas to allow greater access for US cheese producers.

It has also asked for the ban on US alcohol sales, imposed last year by most Canadian provinces in retaliation to Trump's tariffs, be removed.

summary.en: The government in Monrovia says the first batch of 20 people should arrive in Liberia on Thursday. The Trump administration has been seeking countries to take people it cannot send back to their countries of origin.

body.zh: 蒙罗维亚政府表示，第一批 20 人将于周四抵达利比里亚。特朗普政府一直在寻求各国将其无法遣返的人带回原籍国。 利比里亚政府本周表示，该国已同意在未来 12 个月内接收最多 1,200 名来自美国的第三国被驱逐者。 唐纳德·特朗普政府最近与非洲国家达成了几项协议，接收其无法合法送回祖国的人——通常是因为美国法院裁定这样做会将他们置于危险之中。 利比里亚政府在周二发表的一份声明中表示：“利比里亚打算在一年内接受从美国转移的最多 1,200 人。” 声明称，这些人将被“当作客人”接待，他们将“在愿意时自由离开该国”或申请庇护。 政府声明称，被驱逐者“将包括经医疗授权可以旅行的非洲和西半球国家的公民或国民”。 该公司表示，该交易不涉及与美国的交换条件，也没有提出任何要求，也没有获得任何直接补偿。 不过，它还表示将获得“支持来帮助管理该计划并更广泛地加强其移民系统”，但没有详细说明。 声明还提到了利比里亚 19 世纪作为美国奴隶的避难所的历史，以及“接受政治和其他危机寻求庇护的人的悠久历史”。 这一消息是在利比里亚总统约瑟夫·博阿凯与一群非洲领导人一起访问白宫并与特朗普举行会谈大约一年后宣布的。 为了寻求一种方法来驱逐那些无法将其送回原籍国的潜在移民——通常是因为美国法院裁定这样做会使他们面临酷刑或其他虐待的风险——特朗普政府一直在寻求与愿意接收部分移民的第三国达成协议。 美国政府捍卫此类协议的合法性，尽管一些人权组织和倡导者表示，细节往往不透明，而且许多被驱逐者最终被遣返。 除了蒙罗维亚的描述之外，目前还没有关于被驱逐者确切来自哪里的信息。 刚果民主共和国、中非共和国、赤道几内亚、喀麦隆、加纳和塞拉利昂等其他非洲国家也与美国达成了类似协议。 欧盟目前正在研究类似的计划，允许成员国将被拒绝的寻求庇护者送往所谓的“返回中心”......

title.en: India 'Cockroach' movement takes aim at government schools
title.zh: 印度“蟑螂”运动剑指政府学校

summary.en: A student protest movement in India, dubbed the 'Cockroach' movement, is expanding its grassroots efforts into a nationwide campaign. The initiative aims to audit government schools that have been neglected and to pressure authorities to address these issues.
summary.zh: 印度一项名为“蟑螂”的学生抗议运动正将其基层网络发展为全国性行动。该运动旨在审计被忽视的公立学校，并向当局施压，要求其采取行动。

body.en:
The student protest movement is turning its grassroots network into a nationwide campaign to audit neglected government schools and pressure authorities to act.

The student protest movement in India known as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) scored a major victory in July after Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down following weeks of demonstrations in Delhi.

Now, the movement is aiming its campaign for accountability at improving India's government schools.

Last week on India's Independence Day, the CJP launched a nationwide campaign asking citizens to inspect government schools, document what is missing and pressure local authorities to fix basic facilities.

Dubbed "Fix the Schools," the campaign aims to mobilize citizens to identify problems locally and make them public.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke launched a campaign in the Indian state of Maharashtra from his native village in Hingoli district. He spoke with students and documented what he said were broken windows, lack of clean drinking water, missing classroom benches and unusable bathrooms.

"No matter which political party ruled, nobody worked for government schools in states. Now there is a need, and we can make them work by asking questions," said Dipke.

Government officials did not respond to DW's requests for comment on the CJP's accusations.

The CJP has prepared assessment forms that parents, students and residents can use to document issues with local government schools. They are being asked to record video evidence, complete the assessment and send the material to CJP.

The organization plans to compile the reports into a public record of neglected schools and use them to pressure local authorities to respond.

The CJP has said the campaign will focus on five basic requirements: functioning toilets, electricity, clean drinking water, classroom benches and the quality of midday meals.

One element is to publicly recognize village heads who improve their local schools. The CJP plans to use before-and-after evidence to highlight villages where conditions have improved.

The organization has set an initial target of auditing at least 100 rural government schools over the next two months and pressing authorities to act on the findings.

The youth-led CJP began in May as a campaign calling for accountability over a scandal involving a highly competitive university entrance exam. The news that the question sheet had been leaked ahead of the exam date in early May exposed long-running grievances over privileged access for some students.

Fueled by millions of young followers on social media, the movement soon tapped into wider frustrations over unemployment, shrinking opportunities and an education system many young Indians believe has failed them.

title.en: Why the US is going after the International Criminal Court
title.zh: 为什么美国要追究国际刑事法院

summary.en: Marco Rubio, Donald Trump's secretary of state, has announced sanctions against two members of the International Criminal Court, including its president. Rubio's pressure on the court has far-reaching consequences.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Marco Rubio, Donald Trump's secretary of state, has announced sanctions against two members of the International Criminal Court, including its president. Rubio's pressure on the court has far-reaching consequences.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio took aim at the International Criminal Court (ICC)  on Tuesday, calling it "corrupt and fatally politicized" and claiming it has "maliciously abused its authority and exceeded its mandate."

He announced sanctions against the ICC president, Tomoko Akane of Japan, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye of Senegal. The sanctions include freezing of their US-held bank assets and largely cutting them off from the US financial system.

The ICC has been holding individuals accountable for war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity since 2002. The court is based in  The Hague , just like the  International Court of Justice (ICJ) , which is part of the United Nations and settles disputes between states.

Unlike the ICJ, the ICC has 125 members, not all 193 UN member states. The US, Russia and China are among the countries that have not joined, along with several states in Asia and North Africa.

Rubio  had recently threatened to dismantle the court "brick by brick." In a statement in July, the State Department outlined a number of measures Washington is considering as part of its campaign against the court. These include visa restrictions on ICC staff and tougher sanctions targeting the court and affiliated organizations. It also suggested increased scrutiny of countries "that refuse to reject the ICC's illegitimate authority" while continuing to receive US assistance.

The US has clashed with the ICC before . But legal experts around the world say Washington's latest escalation marks a significant shift.

"What the US and Marco Rubio have now essentially done is make public something that has been going on for more than a year," Andreas Schüller, co-director of the International Crimes and Legal Accountability Program at the European Center for Constitutional and Human Rights (ECCHR) in Berlin, told DW in July.

"The US has been using various forms of diplomatic pressure against other countries in an effort to change their positions, and in some cases their voting behavior, toward the ICC," he added.

"The fact that it is now being declared a campaign shows that it is being pursued strategically, that it is broader in scope, and that other countries — including those that are not ICC members — are also being brought on board to help apply pressure."

title.en: Could Pakistan's jailed ex-PM Imran Khan make a new deal?
title.zh: 巴基斯坦被监禁的前总理伊姆兰·汗能否达成新协议？

summary.en: Pakistan's imprisoned former prime minister, Imran Khan, may be transferred to a hospital for medical treatment, leading to speculation about potential new political negotiations.
summary.zh: 巴基斯坦被监禁的前总理伊姆兰·汗可能被转移到医院接受治疗，引发了关于可能进行新政治谈判的猜测。

body.en:
The imprisoned former prime minister of Pakistan could be moved to a hospital for medical treatment, ushering speculation over the possibility of new political negotiations.

Pakistan's Supreme Court on Tuesday ordered jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan to be shifted to a private hospital after Khan's family and political supporters repeatedly raised concerns about the 73-year-old's deteriorating health in Rawalpindi's Adiala jail.

The founder of the opposition party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) has been imprisoned since August 2023 and is currently serving a 14-year sentence on corruption charges he says are politically motivated.

The former prime minister was ousted in a parliamentary no-confidence vote in April 2022. Khan and his supporters say Pakistan's influential military is trying to keep him out of politics, an allegation the military has denied.

Despite remaining behind bars, Khan remains politically popular. After a crackdown on the PTI following Khan's arrest, the candidates backed by him performed strongly in the February 2024 election.

"Three years in prison have not removed Khan from Pakistani politics. He remains PTI's biggest political asset, but the party's reliance on him has also exposed weaknesses in its leadership and organization," Raza Rumi, a US-based Pakistani political analyst, told DW.

The possible transfer of Khan to the Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad for medical assessment has added a new dimension to the debate over his future and the possibility of political negotiations.

However, Khan's adviser Sayed Zulfi Bukhari rejected speculation that the court decision was the result of any political deal with the government.

title.en: 'Power of the purse': What Trump stands to lose in US midterm test
title.zh: “钱袋子”的力量：特朗普在美国中期选举中可能失去什么

summary.en: As midterm primaries continue with elections in several states this week, analysts are predicting a shake-up in the political landscape, indicating potential shifts in influence for former President Trump.

body.en:
The 2026 United States midterm elections will be a crucial test of Donald Trump's political strength, with Democrats hoping to regain control of Congress and Republicans seeking to defy the historical tendency for a president's party to lose ground halfway through a term.

The November elections will determine control of the House of Representatives and could reshape the balance of power in Washington for the final two years of Trump's presidency.

The first midterm primaries were held in March and have continued in recent months, with Alaska, Florida and Wyoming holding their primaries this week.

For Democrats, the November midterms offer an opportunity to demonstrate that dissatisfaction with Trump can translate into electoral gains and to begin rebuilding the party ahead of the next general election in 2028.

For Republicans, the elections will test whether Trump's political strength remains sufficient to protect the party from the historical midterm backlash that has affected many previous administrations.

And for Trump himself, a Democratic-controlled House could mean substantially greater scrutiny, investigations and political resistance during the final years of his presidency.

Wesley Widmaier, a professor at the Australian National University Department of International Relations, told SBS News an overall loss for Trump would restrict his influence.

"The House controls the power of the purse and is where budgets originate in the American system. A Democrat win would mean a loss of a lot of control for Trump," he said.

Ultimately, the midterms could provide the clearest indication yet of whether the political momentum in the US is shifting away from Trump and the Republican Party — or whether Republicans can defy the historical pattern and maintain their grip on Congress.

Every two years, US citizens elect all 435 members of the House of Representatives, while roughly one-third of the Senate is elected.

The House of Representatives has the special power to initiate tax bills and to impeach officials, while the Senate approves presidential appointments, such as judges and cabinet members.

Unlike in Australia, voting in US elections is not compulsory, and midterm elections — those held between presidential elections — tend to have lower voter turnout and less media attention.

But Widmaier said they still have significance for US politics and decision-making.

Historically, the president's party tends to lose ground in the House during midterm elections, he explained.

title.en: Donald Trump says no Iran talks planned, shares map showing Hormuz as 'new US territory'
title.zh: 特朗普称未计划与伊朗谈判，并分享地图将霍尔木兹海峡标为“美国新领土”

summary.en: US President Donald Trump stated that no talks with Iran are planned, while also sharing a map that depicted the Strait of Hormuz as "new US territory." Iran has maintained its stance that it will not reopen the vital waterway unless the US lifts its blockade of Iranian ports.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，目前没有与伊朗进行谈判的计划，同时他还分享了一张地图，将霍尔木兹海峡标注为“美国新领土”。伊朗坚称，除非美国解除对伊朗港口的封锁，否则不会重新开放这条重要的航道。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has said no talks with Iran are underway and none are scheduled, as he posted a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as a new US territory.

Trump has been pressing his threat to claim sovereignty over the crucial energy waterway as the nearly six-month-old Iran war grinds on with little sign of resolution.

Trump's envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner had said on Monday that the US and Iran were having "very positive and active conversations", but the president denied that was the case.

"There are no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled, with the Islamic Republic of Iran. The Naval Blockade remains in full force and effect," Trump wrote on his Truth Social network on Tuesday night.

"The Hormuz Strait is open and operating. All water mines have been removed or detonated."

US sources told the Agence-France Presse news agency there had been "positive" discussions with the Iranians, but added that Trump had decided to wait and asked his team not to engage until Iran was ready to make a deal.

In recent weeks, there has been a lull in fighting, though the United Arab Emirates has recently accused Iran of firing two ballistic missiles — which landed at sea — targeting "maritime navigation." Iran, however, denied firing a missile toward the UAE.

Soon after, the UAE announced that "in light of regional escalations" it was halting all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran.

The UAE bore the brunt of Iranian missile and drone attacks in the first period of the war, but had not reported any attacks since the US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that was meant to halt the fighting.

Earlier on Tuesday, Trump posted a map on Truth Social showing the Strait of Hormuz as a "NEW U.S. Territory".

Iran has effectively shut down the chokepoint , through which a fifth of the world's oil would usually transit, in retaliation for the war launched by the US and Israel in late February.

Trump revisited the idea again earlier in the week in comments to reporters in the Oval Office.

This is not the first time that Trump, faced with a foreign policy obstacle, has threatened to annex foreign territory.

Since returning to power in 2025, he has threatened to make Canada the 51st US state, seize Greenland and Cuba, and has even alluded to taking control of the Gaza Strip, without following through on any of these threats.

Before the Iran war erupted on 28 February, the Strait of Hormuz was an open waterway with free passage.

title.en: Designed to 'exploit' children: Meta faces a historic courtroom reckoning
title.zh: 旨在“剥削”儿童：Meta 面临历史性的法庭审判

summary.en: The trial's outcome could help reshape Facebook and Instagram, and leave Meta with billions of dollars to pay in penalties.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Meta knowingly hooked and exploited children, a United States federal court has heard in the trial of the social media giant on charges that it deliberately made Instagram and Facebook addictive to young users.

In what many experts have called social media's "big tobacco moment," a coalition of US states is demanding Meta pay US$200 billion ($282 billion) in penalties for using technology specifically designed to foster addiction among children in a similar fashion to cigarettes.

Meta "exploited how kids' brains work," California prosecutor Megan O'Neill said in opening arguments, painting Meta's business model as one built to "hook the users, hold them for as long as they can, harvest their data, and then hide the truth from the public".

"It worked especially well for kids," O'Neill added. "Meta needed kids, and it needed to reassure the people who cared about those kids that the kids are safe."

Meta's lawyer, Paul Schmidt, acknowledged that some users were harmed by the networks, but argued that the company had "tried to come up with tools to help them". He argued research showed no clear link between adolescents' social media use and a lack of well-being.

He also said Mark Zuckerberg, Meta's co-founder and CEO, shared the company's desire to improve its services, and not make them dangerous.

"They don't believe they're going to do well if people don't like their service," Schmidt said.

Before the trial began, the company denied all the allegations, insisting it had worked with parents, experts and law enforcement to incorporate protective safeguards for children.

This is not the first case seeking to hold tech companies — including Meta — accountable for these types of issues, but it could become one of the most consequential if it leads to sweeping changes on the platforms.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify, along with Instagram head Adam Mosseri.

Activists, including mothers of children they say were driven to suicide by their social media usage, rallied outside court.

One mother, Lori Schott, called out Zuckerberg and Mosseri, saying they "built one of those most powerful and richest companies in the world... But power does not excuse harm."

This is the first federal trial in what is expected to be a tidal wave of lawsuits also targeting TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube as families, educators and state governments charge them with harming the mental health of young people.

Meta, which has more than three billion users worldwide, is the sole defendant in this case.

body.zh: 美国联邦法院在对这家社交媒体巨头的审判中获悉，Meta 故意诱骗和剥削儿童，指控其故意让 Instagram 和 Facebook 使年轻用户上瘾。 在许多专家所说的社交媒体“烟草大时刻”，美国各州联盟要求 Meta 支付 2000 亿美元（合 2820 亿美元）的罚款，因为它使用了专门设计的技术，以类似于香烟的方式助长儿童成瘾。 加州检察官梅根·奥尼尔在开庭辩论中表示，Meta“利用了孩子们的大脑工作方式”，并将 Meta 的商业模式描述为“吸引用户，尽可能长时间地保留他们，收集他们的数据，然后向公众隐瞒真相”的商业模式。 “这对孩子们尤其有效，”奥尼尔补充道。 “Meta 需要孩子，它需要让关心这些孩子的人放心，孩子们是安全的。” Meta 的律师保罗·施密特 (Paul Schmidt) 承认，一些用户受到了网络的伤害，但辩称该公司“试图推出工具来帮助他们”。他认为研究表明青少年社交媒体的使用与缺乏幸福感之间没有明显的联系。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 他还表示，Meta 的联合创始人兼首席执行官马克·扎克伯格 (Mark Zuckerberg) 与该公司一样希望改善其服务，而不是让它们变得危险。 “如果人们不喜欢他们的服务，他们就不相信自己会做得很好，”施密特说。 在审判开始前，该公司否认了所有指控，坚称其已与家长、专家和执法部门合作，纳入对儿童的保护措施。 这并不是第一个寻求让科技公司（包括 Meta）对此类问题负责的案例，但如果它导致平台上发生彻底的变化，它可能会成为最重要的案例之一。 Meta 创始人兼首席执行官马克·扎克伯格 (Mark Zuckerberg) 以及 Instagram 负责人亚当·莫塞里 (Adam Mosseri) 都是预计出庭作证的明星证人之一。 活动人士在法庭外集会，其中包括一些自称因使用社交媒体而自杀的孩子的母亲。 一位名叫洛里·肖特 (Lori Schott) 的母亲对扎克伯格和莫塞里表示不满，称他们“建立了世界上最强大、最富有的公司之一……但权力并不能成为伤害的借口。” 这是首次联邦审判，预计将出现一波针对 TikTok、Snapchat 和 YouTube 的诉讼浪潮，因为家庭、教育工作者和州政府指控它们损害年轻人的心理健康。 Meta在全球拥有超过30亿用户，是本案的唯一被告。 除了经济处罚外，各州还要求做出改变……

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns
title.zh: 印尼与中国海军演习引发中立担忧

summary.en: Indonesia's participation in a limited naval exercise with China near Taiwan has raised questions about its long-standing nonaligned foreign policy.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚与中国海军在台湾附近举行了有限的海上演习，这引发了对其长期不结盟外交政策的担忧。

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

Kabinawa added that passing exercises were among the lowest-level naval activities yet used by China to justify its intimidation of Taiwan.

body.zh: 印度尼西亚维持不结盟的外交政策，但雅加达有限地参与与中国海军在台湾附近举行的低级别海军演习，引起了密切关注。 8月12日，一艘印度尼西亚护卫舰短暂参加了与中国人民解放军海军在台湾东海岸附近海域举行的海军演习，台北向雅加达询问其参加演习的原因。 印度尼西亚海军护卫舰 KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai 与中国海军导弹护卫舰红河号一起进行了雅加达所说的“穿越演习”。这次演习是在台湾一年一度的汉光军演期间进行的。 印度尼西亚外交部发言人表示，他们完全意识到演习地点“使其特别敏感”，但强调其船只的存在“只是其返回印度尼西亚的过境路线的一部分”。据《台北时报》报道，这艘印尼舰艇在与俄罗斯海军演习后正从俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克返回。 中国8月11日宣布演习后，台湾陆委会谴责北京的“挑衅”。台北还要求外交部“提供更多细节”。 北京认为台湾是中国领土，并誓言要让这个自治岛屿与大陆“统一”，必要时会使用武力。特别是自美国前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 2022 年访问台北以来，解放军在台湾频繁进行军事演习，加大了对台湾的压力。 在台北和华盛顿的反应中，印度尼西亚海军表示，其与中国海军的活动“本质上不是战斗活动”，并且“无意进行战斗训练”。 台湾淡江大学国际事务与战略研究所副教授林英宇告诉德国之声，中国与印尼的演习没有什么战术意义。 他说：“这不像联合海上演习那么实际，但中国希望宣示其在该海域的能力。” 不过，日本国际问题研究所研究台印尼关系的客座研究员拉蒂·卡比纳瓦(Ratih Kabinawa)告诉德国之声，无论演习的意义如何，印尼都应该预料到台湾会做出一些反应。 “无论你喜欢与否，印度尼西亚现在都被拖入了这种地缘政治游戏，”她说。 卡比纳瓦补充说，此次演习是中国迄今为止用来证明其恐吓台湾合理性的最低级别的海军活动之一。 她说：“印度尼西亚在这方面也必须保持谨慎。”她补充说，雅加达应该“不要太天真”，认为参加与中国的“定期演习”不会引起人们的担忧……

body.en:
The Australian government has criticised the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) over its decision not to formally investigate whether crimes were committed by those responsible for killing Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom.

In one of her strongest statements as foreign minister, Penny Wong said "Australia is outraged" at the IDF's decision to close the investigation into the drone strike in Gaza that killed Frankcom and others working for World Central Kitchen .

She confirmed Israel's ambassador in Canberra, Hillel Newman, will be called in for an explanation as the government considers "next steps".

The decision was published on World Humanitarian Day, which Minister Wong said was "especially insulting" to Frankcom’s family and humanitarians across the globe.

She also revealed Israel communicated its decision to the Australian government "moments" before it was publicly announced.

"Australia is outraged the Israeli government has decided not to pursue criminal proceedings against those responsible for killing Zomi Frankcom and her World Central Kitchen colleagues," Wong said.

"The Australian government learned of Israel’s decision late last night, moments before it was announced, on World Humanitarian Day — which is especially insulting to Zomi's loved ones, humanitarians and all Australians."

Israel's military announced on Wednesday night it had completed reviews of 150 incidents of troop conduct in Gaza and made decisions on five cases, including the 1 April 2024 attack on an aid convoy that killed seven aid workers including Frankcom in Khan Younis.

It said it had launched criminal investigations into two high-profile attacks on Palestinians during the war, but not into the April 2024 strike.

The IDF said ‌there was "no ⁠reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct that would justify the opening of a criminal investigation".

The foreign minister said the IDF's response was "far short" of the accountability she expected.

"Zomi represented the best of Australia. Her courage deserves to be celebrated. Her family deserves justice," she said.

“This is despite Israel Defense Forces admissions that the IDF strikes on Zomi and her colleagues’ vehicles were the result of serious failures to follow IDF procedures, mistaken identification and errors in decision-making.

"Democracies seek and accept higher standards. The Australian government will not stop pressing Israel for justice for Zomi and her colleagues."

The Australian government and Frankcom's family have long demanded transparency and accountability from Israel over her death.

body.en:
Australians are sitting on about $4.4 trillion in superannuation savings for retirement. But there are ongoing debates about whether they should be allowed to access some of that money early to help with costs of living.

And making an early withdrawal can have a big potential impact on your future retirement savings — especially if you are in your 20s or 30s.

So what are the rules around early withdrawal, and who do you have to convince if you're making a claim?

Superannuation savings are intended to help people cover their living expenses when they have left the workforce and are in retirement.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Taxes on super contributions are lower than income tax rates, and withdrawals after retirement are also at discounted tax rates.

Those low tax rates come with strings attached: rules that prevent people from using their superannuation savings for other reasons than income in retirement.

For the most part, superannuation savings in Australia are not readily withdrawn until at least age 60. People can withdraw super from age 60 if they have stopped working, or from age 65 even if they have not stopped working.

But the rules are strict. And who you need to apply to will depend on your reasons for seeking to withdraw money.

For instance, if you apply on compassionate grounds, you need to apply via the tax office and meet all of its criteria.

But in other circumstances, such as severe financial hardship, you need to apply directly through your super fund. Even if you meet all the criteria — which includes having received government income support payments for at least half a year — it's up to the fund trustees' discretion whether to say yes. The most you can withdraw for severe financial hardship is $10,000 in one year.

People often wish they could access their super for help with house deposits or home loan repayments. First home buyers may be eligible for the First Home Super Saver scheme. But in general, just needing help for mortgage repayments is not going to be sufficient grounds to access your super savings.

The tax office has had to issue warnings about misleading ads and social media claims, encouraging people to try to withdraw super on compassionate grounds, such as medical or dental expenses that are not absolutely necessary on health grounds.

The tax office says to be particularly careful with anyone suggesting super can be accessed to pay for cosmetic or elective procedures, as these treatments usually aren’t eligible.

If someone offers to help you apply to your super fund to take money out, that’s a red flag. It could even be a scam.

body.en:
At Steven Law's home in Northcote, Melbourne, family albums are strewn across the dining room table, offering glimpses into a past that was rarely discussed.

A large sepia photograph catches Steven's eye and he lifts a magnifying glass to look more closely.

It features a woman — Steven's grandmother Irene Law — wearing a large hat and a scarf draped around her shoulders. It is just the way Steven remembers her.

"Irene was an elegant woman; she was well spoken, well dressed. That was how we knew her," Steven told SBS Chinese.

Decades after her death, her image has appeared on walls across Australia, as part of artist Peter Drew’s Aussie poster series — bringing a little-known chapter of her life into view and raising questions about who gets to be called Australian.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

When Steven's sister Christina Law discovered that her grandmother would feature in Drew's poster collection, she was moved to tears.

"I was really overwhelmed and quite teary when I saw that nanna had been included in this series," Christina told SBS Chinese.

The posters feature archival photographs, sourced from the National Archives of Australia (NAA) of people who applied for certificates exempting them from the dictation test .

Under the Immigration Restriction Act 1901, one of the laws that formed part of what is now known as the White Australia policy, the dictation test could be administered at an officer's discretion to people seeking entry to Australia.

It required a person to write a 50-word passage in a European language dictated by an immigration officer. After 1905, the officer could choose "any prescribed language", making it possible to administer the test in a language the person did not understand.

People who failed were declared a "prohibited immigrant" and refused entry or , in some circumstances, deported .

The exemption certificates were designed to allow eligible non-European residents who had lived in Australia to leave temporarily and return within a set timeframe without being subjected to the dictation test.

The posters have since sparked mixed reactions, including graffiti, counter-posters and attempts to tear them down.

In recent months, videos of the artworks being defaced and altered to include different messages about identity have also circulated on social media.

"Someone has vandalised my old posters, so I've got some new ones, and I'm going to fix them up," Drew told SBS Chinese while standing on Morphett Street in Adelaide's central business district.

title.en: 'Left feeling like a burden': How the government's new NDIS changes may impact you
title.zh: “感到自己是负担”：政府新的NDIS改革可能如何影响你

summary.en: The National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) in Australia is undergoing changes, prompting concerns that these reforms may lead some participants to feel like a burden.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚的国家残疾保险计划（NDIS）即将进行改革，引发了人们的担忧，认为这些变化可能让一些参与者感到自己成为负担。

body.en:
An overhaul of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) has passed the Senate with Coalition support, sent back to the Labor-controlled lower house to be rubber-stamped.

Analysis by the Grattan Institute suggests hundreds of thousands of people will be moved off the scheme or prevented from joining under the changes.

Applicants will be assessed in stages under a new test to determine their functional capacity.

That test is still being developed and will replace the current diagnosis-based model.

Acting CEO of peak body People With Disability Australia Megan Spindler-Smith says her community is grieving.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"There will be harm, there will be injuries. What we're talking about here is that when you reduce people's access to the supports that they need to be able to get out of bed, access the community, go to work, you ostensibly isolate people."

She says many lives will be made smaller by the reforms — which will slash social and community participation supports in half.

"The support needs don't go away when the funding is cut or when the supports are removed. They just get pushed onto either systems or other people, and that means isolation."

Since it started in 2013, the cost of the scheme has ballooned, rising to $50 billion dollars this year, and projected to hit $100 billion within a decade.

The government says its overhaul will slow the scheme’s growth and save almost $38 billion over the next four years.

Greens MPs like Jordon Steele-John say the focus on financial cost has made many disabled people feel like a burden.

“Many people, during the course of this debate, while the government has been trying to push this legislation through, have shared with me that they have felt as though they are being talked about in a way that leaves them feeling like a burden, and that is just not okay.”

Health Minister Mark Butler says reining in spending growth was necessary to safeguard the scheme's financial sustainability and social license.

"This plan puts the scheme back on track, and I'm confident, secures it for decades to come," Butler said.

"It genuinely has transformed the lives of hundreds of thousands of people, and I want to continue to see that happen for decades to come. reflection.en: When policy changes affect vulnerable members of society, it is crucial to ensure their dignity and voice are upheld. Yahweh calls us to speak up for those who may feel marginalized or unheard, advocating for their inherent worth and rights. title.en: Why a 52-metre SpaceX rocket ended up off the coast of Christmas Island
title.zh: 为何一枚 52 米长的 SpaceX 火箭最终坠入圣诞岛海岸

summary.en: The rocket's arrival at the remote island caused a stir among the locals.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Elon Musk's aerospace company SpaceX has retrieved a rocket that splashed down in the Indian Ocean near Christmas Island.

The space debris was towed to the remote island, about 1,500 kilometres off north-west Western Australia, on Tuesday.

"After approx. 24 days at sea, the SpaceX Recovery team successfully guided Starship to a location just off the coast of Christmas Island," the US aerospace manufacturer and launch services company said in a social media post.

"A team of SpaceX engineers is on their way to conduct additional analysis on the vehicle in calmer waters before attempting to return it to Starbase."

Locals in the remote territory reportedly lined up along the rugged coastline to catch a glimpse of the 52-metre-long rocket as it was towed in.

Photographer Chris Bray, who usually focuses on wildlife, said it was not something he ever expected to see.

"This SpaceX Starship was towed into the protected waters around Christmas Island this morning after an unusually gentle landing in the Indian Ocean almost a month ago left it unexpectedly floating and potentially recoverable instead of the usual explosion!" he said on an Instagram post on Tuesday.

Bray's aerial photos show the mostly black-coloured rocket being towed by cable attached to two large ships.

The rocket, which has three large and three small rocket nozzles, appears to have lost some of its outer coating, but was otherwise intact.

The SpaceX website said the company's Starship spacecraft and super heavy rocket were a reusable transport system designed to carry crew and cargo into "orbit, the moon, Mars and beyond".

In 2023, a large gold-coloured dome-like object was found on a beach about 250km north of Perth.

The Australian Space Agency later concluded it was an expended third stage of a polar satellite launch vehicle operated by the Indian Space Research Organisation.

In 1979, parts of NASA's Skylab space station crashed to earth near the sleepy towns of Esperance and Balladonia, triggering a global media frenzy.
